test_title: PYST 57: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which stance did the Reserve Bank of India adopt after the April 2025 repo rate cut?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Accommodative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** adopts an **Accommodative** stance when it aims to expand the **money supply** to boost **economic growth**. This stance is typically characterized by a willingness to either keep the **Repo Rate** unchanged or reduce it further.
 
• Following the **April 2025** monetary policy review, the decision to cut the **Repo Rate** was a clear indicator of this stance, intended to lower **borrowing costs** for both consumers and businesses.
 
• An **Accommodative** stance signals to the **financial markets** that the central bank is prioritizing **liquidity injection** and **investment** over immediate concerns regarding **inflationary pressures**, provided **inflation** remains within the **tolerance band**.
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, which consists of **six members**, evaluates various **macroeconomic indicators** such as **GDP growth** and the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** before deciding on such a shift in stance.
 
• By maintaining this stance, the **RBI** ensures that **commercial banks** have sufficient **liquidity** to provide **loans** at cheaper rates, thereby stimulating **aggregate demand** in the **Indian economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body established under **Section 45ZB** of the amended **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It is chaired by the **Governor of the RBI** and is responsible for fixing the **benchmark policy rate** (Repo Rate) to contain **inflation** within the specified **target level**.
 
• The committee meets at least **four times a year**, and its decisions are published after every meeting.
 
 
 
• **Types of Monetary Policy Stances:**
 
 
• **Neutral Stance:** This implies that the **RBI** can move the **interest rates** in either direction (increase or decrease) based on **incoming data**.
 
• **Hawkish/Restrictive Stance:** The central bank focuses on curbing **inflation** by **increasing interest rates** and reducing the **money supply**.
 
• **Withdrawal of Accommodation:** This indicates a transition where the **RBI** starts reducing the **liquidity** it had previously pumped into the system, moving toward a **neutral** or **tight** policy.
 
 
 
• **Important Instruments of Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• **Repo Rate:** The **interest rate** at which the **RBI** lends money to **commercial banks** against **government securities**.
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:** The **rate** at which the **RBI** borrows money from **commercial banks** within the country.
 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR):** The specific **percentage** of **net demand and time liabilities (NDTL)** that **banks** must keep with the **RBI** in the form of **cash**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inflation Targeting:** The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, set an **inflation target** of **4%** with a **flexibility band** of **+/- 2%** (i.e., between **2%** and **6%**).
 
• **Economic Impact:** A cut in the **Repo Rate** usually leads to a decrease in **Equated Monthly Installments (EMIs)** for **home loans**, **car loans**, and **personal loans**, provided the **transmission of rates** by **banks** is efficient.
 
• **Liquidity Management:** Under an **Accommodative** stance, the **RBI** often uses **Open Market Operations (OMO)** to buy **government bonds**, thereby increasing the **cash flow** in the **banking system**.
 
• **Global Context:** The **RBI's** stance in **2025** is also influenced by **global economic conditions**, including the **monetary policy** of the **US Federal Reserve** and **international crude oil prices**.
</ul
